fullName.value: Phosphorylase b kinase regulatory subunit beta

texts.value: Phosphorylase b kinase catalyzes the phosphorylation of serine in certain substrates, including troponin I. The beta chain acts as a regulatory unit and modulates the activity of the holoenzyme in response to phosphorylation
By phosphorylation of various serine residues

Hexadecamer of 4 heterotetramers, each composed of alpha, beta, gamma, and delta subunits. Alpha (PHKA1 or PHKA2) and beta (PHKB) are regulatory subunits, gamma (PHKG1 or PHKG2) is the catalytic subunit, and delta is calmodulin
Ser-701 is probably phosphorylated by PKA
Although the final Cys may be farnesylated, the terminal tripeptide is probably not removed, and the C-terminus is not methylated

disease.description: A metabolic disorder characterized by hepatomegaly, only slightly elevated transaminases and plasma lipids, clinical improvement with increasing age, and remarkably no clinical muscle involvement. Biochemical observations suggest that this mild phenotype is caused by an incomplete holoenzyme that lacks the beta subunit, but that may possess residual activity.

texts.value: The disease is caused by variants affecting the gene represented in this entry
Belongs to the phosphorylase b kinase regulatory chain family
